name: MA-03
label: Safe D

key_factors: Trahan holds a massive financial edge: $1.8 million on hand versus roughly $6,000 for Grossi
District leans Democratic by about 11 points on the partisan vote index

model.rationale: Every visible signal points the same way: a Democratic-leaning seat, an established incumbent, and a fundraising gap of more than two hundred to one, with markets pricing Trahan near certain to win. With no polls or ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the only real uncertainty is the size of her margin.
model.watch: A late influx of outside spending against Trahan or an unforeseen scandal could narrow the margin, though nothing in the current evidence suggests either is likely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lori Trahan seeks another term in a Massachusetts district that leans Democratic by about eleven points on the partisan vote index. She has raised more than $1.6 million and holds roughly $1.8 million on hand, while Republican Gary Grossi has reported about $7,000 in receipts. An independent candidate appears on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign finance activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets price Democratic chances around 95 percent, slightly below what the fundamentals alone would suggest but still firmly in safe territory. The combination of a Democratic-leaning seat, an established incumbent, and an overwhelming financial edge makes Trahan a heavy favorite; the realistic uncertainty concerns the size of her margin rather than who wins.
